$comment: HAND-TRANSCRIBED, and every row here is an EXPLICIT NON-PRICE. Not one atlascloud model ships a
`cost` in src/providers/atlascloud/models.ts, and this file is the recorded reason.
ONE FIGURE PER MODEL, AND ATLAS'S OWN PAGES SAY IT IS NOT A RATE (all read 2026-11-12). The model
page's markdown form (https://www.atlascloud.ai/models/<id>/llms.txt) states one figure and calls
it authoritative — "These are the authoritative Atlas Cloud rates for this model." over "- $0.2
per second of generated video" (google/veo3.1/text-to-video) — and the HTML meta description
agrees ("Starting from $0.134/second", bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video). Three other
Atlas sources say that figure is not the price of a request:
1. the billing page, https://www.atlascloud.ai/docs/models/price: video pricing "Varies by
model, duration, and resolution; some models are billed by output video tokens", and
"Image/Video generation is charged per request; failed tasks are automatically not charged";
2. Atlas's own cost test, https://www.atlascloud.ai/blog/tips/seedance-2-5-draft-mode-cost-test:
"A 480p draft is ready in about 1 min 40 s at $0.134 per second" and "Upgrading to 1080p
costs $0.592 per second, almost the same as $0.596 for direct 1080p." — one model, one day,
"including that day's 20% discount". The page's figure is the floor of an unpublished
resolution ladder; a flat per-second rate would under-state direct 1080p about 4.4x;
3. the page bundle, which still ships a per-run and a per-1000-token template ("Your request
will cost ${price} per run. For $10 you can run this model approximately {times} times.",
and "... per 1000 tokens. The number of tokens is given by (height of output video x width
of output video x (input duration + output duration) x 24) / 1024 ..."); which one renders
for a given model cannot be read without executing the page.
AND THE CATALOG CANNOT SETTLE IT. GET https://api.atlascloud.ai/api/v1/models (608 rows, read
2026-11-12) returns a `price` object per row, but NONE of the 31 curated rows carries
`price.actual.unit`, and 389 of its 470 media rows are a bare `base_price` STRING with no unit at
all. And 223 of 608 rows carry a promotional `discount` between 30 and 95, so `price.actual` is
not the list price either — it is today's offer.
SO EVERY ROW IS `unpriced`, under the same rule that governs data/fal/pricing.json: a rate needs a
source, a date and the quote it was read from, or the row ships no rate. What is carried instead is
what Atlas actually published — `listed.actual`, `listed.origin` and `listed.discount`, transcribed
verbatim and explicitly UNIT-LESS. `src/providers/atlascloud/pricing.ts` re-states the same table
as ATLASCLOUD_LISTED_BASE_PRICE_USD beside ATLASCLOUD_PRICING_CAVEAT, and
`atlascloud.video` declares NO `estimate` at all — a function that always returns `undefined` is a
promise that a number is coming, and a missing one is the truth.
READ `listed.discount` CAREFULLY: it is Atlas's own field and 100 means NO discount (actual ===
origin). 80 means the row is currently discounted to 80% of list. It is a percentage OF the list
price, not off it.
WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS, so the next reader knows the diff is small: Atlas publishing the
per-resolution ladder its billing page describes, with a `price.actual.unit` on the curated rows.
The transcription is already here; only the `unpriced` reason would come out and a `unit` + `usd`
pair go in.
Row shape:
unpriced  the REASON no rate can be stated, in prose. Present on every row today.
listed    { actual, origin, discount } — Atlas's own numbers, unit unknown.
source / verified
`bun run audit:atlascloud` re-reads the catalog weekly and reports when a listed figure moves.
